title: Simplify Path
statement: Convert an absolute Unix path to its canonical form. '.' means the current directory, '..' means the parent, and multiple slashes are one separator. The result starts with a single slash.
hints: Split on '/'. Empty tokens come from repeated slashes and are ignored.
'.' is ignored. '..' pops a directory if the stack is not empty. You cannot go above the root.
Join the stack with slashes and prefix the root slash.

approaches.name: String replace
approaches.explanation: Fragile around repeated slashes and dot segments.

approaches.name: Stack of directory names
approaches.explanation: One token decides push, pop, or skip.

editorial: The stack is the sequence of real directories still on the path. Tokens that are empty or '.' do not change it. '..' pops when possible. Every other token is a directory name and is pushed. The canonical path is '/' joined with the stack, or '/' when the stack is empty.
